newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks non-committal on plans to buy Mack.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks non-committal on plans to buy Mack.

text.p: Volvo Trucks, a unit of Sweden's Volvo, Tuesday would neither confirm nor deny a Swedish newspaper report that it planned to buy U.S. truckmaker Mack from French vehicle maker Renault.
"We don't plan any other cooperation than the discussions we are having with Mitsubishi," Volvo Trucks spokesman Kjell Drotz told Reuters.
Asked if an acquisition of Mack could be seen as something other than cooperation, he said: "That is not the way you should interpret it."
Drotz admitted, however, that Volvo Trucks was looking at different strategies and scenarios.

Daily Svenska Dagbladet reported Tuesday that Volvo Trucks planned to buy Mack to meet its target of 20 percent of the U.S. truck market. Volvo Trucks currently has a 10 percent market share and Mack 8.8 percent.
"The deal would double Volvo's market share and give it access to Mack's network of retailers and service plants in the U.S.," the newspaper said.

But the report said the deal faced complications. It noted that while Renault might think of selling Mack, Volvo would also have to take over Renault's previously troubled European truck operations, which it said Volvo was not interested in doing.
